summary: Phase 2 Independent review audit at c095ba1f. HEAD equals the audited SHA. The phase diff 3e8d29e8..c095ba1f touches only the 13 phase-owned paths: check-review.sh, red-p2.log, green-p2.log, four vision-review batch JSONs and four batch logs, plan.md Phase 2 lines, and scenes/inventory.md. The TSV, docs/map-review.html, scenes/maps/, docs/map-mockups/, and bench/ are unchanged in the range (git diff --exit-code empty). The gate rerun passes: check-review.sh exits 0 with 34 checks (PASS=34, FAIL=0), matching plan.md:57-58 word for word, and the plan gate lists four JSON files. An independent node cross-check of all 30 inventory rows against the four batch JSONs found 0 mismatches on rating (numeric compare), critical flag, judge note, judge route cell, and state cell rated in last position; the slug set equals the 30 civic P2 TSV slugs with an empty symmetric difference. All 30 MAPS rating and note cells are byte-identical to the Phase 1 version at 3e8d29e8 (0 differences). The P2-c route reading agrees with test-strategy.md section 5: the checker rejects claude/anthropic/sonnet in both model_family and the route string, and my live fixture probe confirmed a claude-family judge fails P2-c. A3 and A4 defenses hold by live probes: a date-string rating fails P2-b, a dropped map fails P2-a with 5 FAILs. The by-design check-inventory.sh failure was rerun: exit 1 with 96 checks (PASS=6, FAIL=90), exactly as plan.md:63-64 records. Every plan evidence claim at plan.md:37, 42, and 52 to 64 was re-verified against live command output. Three nonblocking findings remain: P2-d never verifies the Judge critical cell or the judge route cell (fixture proof: both mutations pass 34/34), the P2-c log-citation model-id grep is vacuous because the route string contains the model id, and the by-design check-inventory.sh failure has consequences for later gates that the plan should carry forward.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Nit] review-a-p2 check-review.sh P2-d (measure/runs/asset_scenes_civic_20260928/check-review.sh:211-265): the P2-d loop verifies the state cell, the Judge rating, and the Judge note, but never reads the Judge critical cell or the judge route cell, while plan.md:59 claims the rows hold the judge route and the copied rating, critical flag and note. Fixture proof: an inventory copy with mill's Judge critical cell flipped to false passes 34/34 exit 0, and a copy with mill's judge cell set to anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 also passes 34/34 exit 0. The committed inventory is faithful (independent node check: 30 rows, 0 mismatches on all five cells), so the exposure is future drift only. The critical flag matters downstream: the Phase 3 rework set is maps below 7.0 or critical, so a false critical cell on a 7.0-or-above map with a true batch critical would drop it from Phase 3. Mill itself is double-covered (5.5 and critical true).

F2 [Nit] review-a-p2 check-review.sh P2-c log check (measure/runs/asset_scenes_civic_20260928/check-review.sh:202-208): the branch { grep -qF "$MODEL" "$LOG" || grep -qiF "$FAM" "$LOG" } is always true once grep -qF "$ROUTE" passes, because the route string contains the model id as a substring. The pass line claims the log cites its route and a model id or family, but the test reduces to the log contains the route. The committed logs are true records: all four carry explicit route and model_id lines (vision-review-b1.log lines 2-3, b2.log line 3, b3.log lines 2-3, b4.log lines 3-4), so only the test label overstates coverage.

F3 [Nit] review-a-p2 by-design check-inventory.sh failure and later gates (measure/runs/asset_scenes_civic_20260928/check-inventory.sh, plan.md:63-64): check-inventory.sh now exits 1 with 96 checks (PASS=6, FAIL=90) because it asserts Phase 1 semantics (judge: no, state inventoried) against rated rows. That failure is correct by design and the plan records it exactly. Consequence for later gates: the Phase 1 closeout rerun is permanently red after Phase 2 (its acceptance is pinned at 3e8d29e8, so the historical record stays intact); each phase checker is phase-bound, so Phase 3's state changes will make check-review.sh P2-d fail by design in the same way, and the final inventory validation rests on the Phase 3 and Phase 4 checkers plus the doctor (P4-f). The plan should add the analogous by-design note for check-review.sh when Phase 3 runs. One of the 90 FAILs (inn says missing but its source exists) is not state drift but the Phase 1 F2 latent substring defect surfacing on the inn MAPS note missing hanging lantern; harmless inside a by-design failure.
